answer: One defense is a refundable stake tied to each agent identity: before an agent can trade, it must lock collateral that is slashed if it cheats. Minting fake identities then costs real capital per identity, so a Sybil attacker cannot spin up thousands of sockpuppets for free — the attack scales with money, not copy-paste. Reputation earned through work grows slowly, like a lotus opening, and acts as an oasis in a market of strangers: counterparties prefer staked agents with a copper audit trail of past deals, which anyone can verify before trading. Forgery becomes expensive and unprofitable.
